title: Safer sync — keeping your files and your choices

steps.headline: Should I fix safety first, then simplify sync without replacing it?
steps.today: Live sync and additional backups use separate jobs. They disagree about pause and success, and some failure paths can remove recovery copies or mishandle files.
steps.problem: A full rewrite would change many working behaviors at once. Tiny isolated patches would leave the duplicated rules that caused several problems.
steps.proposal: Use staged fixes: first protect files and honor existing controls; then share backup rules and truthful status; finally review explanations in the existing interface. Preserve all current features, file coverage and normal deletion behavior unless a later answer explicitly changes them.

options.label: Safety-first batches
pros: Each safety fix gets a reproducing test and independent review.
Keeps familiar controls while removing duplicated rules.
cons: Several review checkpoints rather than one big replacement.

options.label: Safety fixes only
pros: Smallest immediate change to working behavior.
cons: Duplicated backup rules and broader usability issues remain for later.

options.label: Redesign first
pros: Reconsiders the complete sync experience together.
cons: Delays safety fixes and puts more working behavior at risk.

steps.path: A synced project folder, or a stored conversation
steps.headline: Should this pass add new deletion controls, or make existing behavior safe and explicit first?
steps.today: Ordinary synced file deletions propagate. Missing conversation copies can return from another copy, and deleting an active project's whole folder can trigger a download again. Stop syncing keeps the folder.
steps.problem: A missing file does not tell us whether you deliberately erased it, cleared local storage, lost access to a drive, or suffered a failed download.
steps.proposal: First stop repair and cleanup from inventing deletions, and explain existing behavior. A new Remove from this device or Delete everywhere action would be a separate visible design with confirmation and recovery rules, not a hidden change to ordinary file deletion.

options.label: Secure existing actions first
pros: No surprise change to which deletions reach other devices.
Keeps automatic conversation preservation while fixing unsafe failures.
cons: Explicit remove-local and delete-everywhere controls remain a follow-up.

options.label: Design deletion controls too
pros: Users could explicitly choose local removal versus deletion across devices.
cons: Needs additional UI review and decisions about offline devices, recovery and old backups.

steps.headline: Should cleanup keep the last good backup even when it exceeds the normal age limit?
steps.today: Project and conversation backups expire after 30 days. Personal settings backups thin out over time and expire after 90 days. Cleanup can run even when the new backup failed.
steps.problem: Deleting old copies on schedule can leave no usable backup when copying is broken. Keeping them longer consumes storage and retains older deleted content longer.
steps.proposal: Keep the current age schedules for healthy backups, but do not remove the last verified recovery copy or prune after a failed replacement. Pause must stop both copying and cleanup. Existing backups without proof of completion need conservative handling, not guessed success.

options.label: Prioritize recovery
pros: A failed backup cannot erase the remaining verified recovery option.
cons: Some older data remains longer and uses more storage until backups recover.

options.label: Keep strict age limits
pros: Old backup content expires on its current schedule.
cons: All recovery copies can expire during a prolonged backup failure; this must be clearly explained.

steps.path: Settings → Backup & Sync; Projects → Stop syncing
steps.headline: Should sync explanations stay in the existing screens, with details available when needed?
steps.today: The panel can report All synced after an unsuccessful network attempt. Large-file exclusions are not clearly shown, and conflict instructions misidentify which version is the named copy.
steps.problem: Users cannot reliably tell what reached another device, what was excluded, or what stopping and cleanup will do.
steps.proposal: Keep the current layout and controls. Show truthful progress and last-success information, persistent conflict and excluded-file details, and concise consequences beside stop and backup controls. Show you before-and-after mockups before changing the interface.

options.label: Improve existing screens
pros: Important facts appear where users make the decision.
cons: A small amount of additional detail needs room in the existing panel.

options.label: Correct wording only
cons: Finding affected files and understanding incomplete backups remains difficult.
